note: why do i want to see 2 second clips of a man and a dirty shoe? what's the selling point? what's supposed to grab my attention?
means: The opening must dramatise the CLAIM, not depict the category. A dirty shoe is the category and nobody stops for a category. Every one of these films already HAS a claim in its copy - 'most notebooks do not close flat', 'most desk lamps have one setting: on', 'the first mile is easy, anyone can sell you the first mile' - and every one of them illustrates the product sitting still while the words do the arguing. A claim shot has a villain and a resolution IN THE FRAME.
rule: Write the opening keyframe from the film's own first line. If the line names a problem, the picture is the problem. Notebooks that will not close flat: show them springing open. A lamp with one setting: show the glare and the hard shadow it throws. Never open on the product at rest.
evidence: controlled pair, same product/style/grade/seed, only the SUBJECT of the keyframe varying. paperlight: a closed notebook on a table, against a stack with pages fanning open beside one lying flat. lumen: a lamp on a desk, against a bare lamp glaring into a black void. Judged by looking - the claim frames are pictures of an argument, the subject frames are pictures of an object.
status: applied to the demo pair; the slate's openings are still subject-led
